description:
FILED s406 (Opus 5), found by the #337 `my sub` probe battery (the probe used a
sub named `x`, which is how it surfaced).

SILENT WRONG, rc 0, no output:

    sub x { "PKG" }
    print x(), "|\n";        # perl: PKG|      PCL: prints NOTHING

PCL reads the bareword `x` in print's argument list as the REPETITION OPERATOR
and emits

    (p-str-x (p-print $_) (progn))

i.e. `(print $_) x ()` — the print of $_ repeated zero times.  Nothing is
printed and nothing is announced.

NARROW, and probed (scratchpad lexsub/x1.pl):
    my $r = x();            OK   (both "V-x")
    my @l = (x(), 1);       OK   ("PKG 1")
    $obj->x                 OK   (7)
    print((x()), "|\n");    OK   ("PKG|")
    print x(), "|\n";       WRONG (silent)
Only the LIST-OPERATOR argument position diverges.  Every other operator-shaped
name (eq lt gt le ge ne cmp and or xor) is a perl COMPILE ERROR as a sub name,
so `x` and `not` are the only two members of the family that are legal perl at
all; `not` is fine today (probed).

LAYER: this is the `_is_print_term_start` family CLAUDE.md rule 11 names — the
print/say/printf list-operator argument scanner has to decide "term or
operator" for a bareword, and #266's rule applies: a bare NAME is a CALL only
where it is CALLABLE.  Here the name IS callable (a sub of that name is
declared and it is followed by `(`), so the term reading wins.  Fix in the ONE
shared print-argument scanner, never per call path.

BAR: the four working shapes above stay working, `$a x 3` / `($a) x 3` / `"-" x
5` after print (`print "-" x 5, "\n"`) keep parsing as repetition — that is the
case a widening would BREAK, so probe it first — plus a Pl/t row per side.


FIXED s406 (32094da).  It was TWO bugs under one probe:
  1. PPI lexes the call as the repetition operator (ppi-upstream-bugs.md §19,
     report Bug 16, canary in misc-fixes-02.t).  Repair: _repair_word_x_call
     inserts a unary + (perl's own disambiguator, which PCL already emits as a
     plain call) when the Word before `x` is not a DECLARED term.
     _word_is_term now delegates to a new _word_is_declared_term, so the
     ALL-CAPS half of the rule has one copy and the `x` site can opt out of it
     (an ALL-CAPS word before `x` is a filehandle, not a constant).
  2. PCL's own older bug, found by the same probes: `print FOO . "b"`,
     `print FOO - 1`, `print FOO x 3`, `print FOO == 3 ? ...` were DROPPED
     WHOLE, because every ALL-CAPS bareword after print was read as a
     filehandle.  The print branch now asks _is_zero_arg_func (the predicate
     parse()'s bareword branch already used inline).

MEASURED: 17 shapes vs perl, all identical (7 were wrong).  corpus-diff
IDENTICAL 111; emission-ab over perl's t/ 605 files = 604 SAME / 1 DIFF —
t/op/lexsub.t, where two `is x, 3, ...` statements stop being drops (census
8 -> 6).  Gate 147/5355.  Generation v2-150 + all three artifacts regenerated
(one-line stamp diffs); pack.t 5636/89, 0 new.
subject: SILENT WRONG: `print x(), ...` with a sub named x is read as the repetition operator - prints nothing, rc 0
